claims.source_value:
What are the tools supposed to do, then?

Not save me, and certainly not testify that I am a good person. They are supposed to make some of my favorite evasions more difficult. Crucible takes a thesis apart and asks what would refute each claim. Forum preserves a causal record of what agents did. EMET witnesses the bytes instead of treating a signature as moral authority. Gather tries to keep the source boundary visible. Learn keeps the human involved because I do not want a machine that makes me faster while I become less capable of understanding what I am doing.

A person can build a smoke alarm and still light the house on fire.
claims.supports: The author connects tool design with human learning and review.

claims.source_value:
## 2. The verdict lattice (closed)

Every integrity judgement EMET emits MUST be exactly one of: MATCH, DRIFT, or
UNVERIFIABLE.

This enum is CLOSED. An implementation MUST NOT define, emit, or accept any other
verdict -- in particular it MUST NOT emit TRUSTED, APPROVED, or SAFE, or any
value asserting authority or permission. Absence of DRIFT is reported as MATCH
(re-derivation agreed) or UNVERIFIABLE (no raw-byte anchor), never as trust. This
is boundary 1 -- facts, not authority -- encoded in the output type itself.
claims.supports: The closed core integrity verdicts do not grant authority or permission.
